title: Guide, Verify, Solve — Anirban Chatterjee, Sonar
talk_summary: A Sonar product-marketing talk arguing that AI-generated code creates persistent 'verification debt' (rising static-analysis warnings and complexity after the initial productivity spike) and that teams need a zero-trust, multi-layered, independent verification regime in both the inner agent loop and the outer CI/CD loop. The concrete mechanism is a Guide/Verify/Solve loop: feed agents scoped context and constraints up front, run independent computational plus LLM verification (with a quality gate that blocks merge), then let agents fix their own findings and re-verify.

takeaways.technique: Independent computational verification alongside LLM review (multi-layered, zero-trust)
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a deterministic static-analysis/computational pass in addition to LLM review, and require a passing grade across quality, security and maintainability before a PR can proceed; explicitly use a different methodology than the one that wrote the code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Use a different methodology to review the code that was used to write the code.
takeaways.numbers: CMU study: productivity spike lasted ~3 months, then reverted, with persistent increase in static-analysis warnings and code complexity.

takeaways.technique: Quality gate with explicit encoded criteria and pass/fail blocking
takeaways.what_they_do: Encode acceptable levels of security, quality and maintainability as written criteria up front, then have the gate assign grades and refuse to let the PR pass unless it meets them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: won't allow the PR to go past into production unless it gets a passing grade across that criteria

takeaways.technique: In-loop verification: agent calls a verifier mid-task and fixes before proceeding
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose verification as a tool the coding agent calls after each write; it gets a list of issues in real time, fixes them immediately, and re-runs analysis until it passes, so defects don't propagate into later loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will not proceed until it actually is able to get a passing grade from us on the verification pass

takeaways.technique: Scoped context injection instead of dumping the whole codebase
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide only the context relevant to the specific task so the agent doesn't thrash exploring and burn tokens; context is fetched per-task rather than preloaded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You have to manage the context window of the agent you can't just throw your entire code base at the agent up front.

takeaways.what_they_do: Point an agent at accumulated backlog issues and legacy code to fix them in the background, using idle capacity, while humans/agents focus on new work.

takeaways.technique: Human/LLM review is unreliable — backstop with automation, don't trust rubber stamps
takeaways.what_they_do: Cite evidence that reviewers follow confident-but-wrong AI advice ~80% of the time, so automated independent verification must backstop human/LLM review rather than relying on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they unfortunately also listened to the AI nearly 80% of the time when the AI was wrong
takeaways.numbers: Wharton study: participants followed correct AI advice 92.7% of the time and wrong AI advice ~80% of the time.
